turn2.text: Make it more comfortable, budget is less of a concern

input.topic: quiet non-touristy islands anchorages harbours comfortable stays Croatia sailing

picks: Charter: a skippered catamaran or crewed yacht with air-conditioning, a hostess or cook if available, and a short daily sailing leg. This is my general recommendation, not sourced.
Stiniva cove, Vis: a quiet cove, best reached by boat early in the morning.
Vlaka bay, Pakleni islands: a quiet anchorage with a family konoba.
Comfort: a sun awning, plenty of water and kid-sized life jackets. Finish each day's sail before the afternoon wind.
Comfortable stays: add one or two nights in a good hotel ashore in Split or Hvar. I haven't verified any specific hotel, so check before booking.
input.summary: For more comfort, switch to a skippered crewed charter or a roomy catamaran with air-conditioned cabins out of Split or Trogir. Sail in the morning and be anchored before the afternoon maestral (10-15 kn) builds a choppy sea, and plan shade and water for 27-30 °C days. The insider named two quiet stops, Stiniva cove on Vis and Vlaka bay in the Pakleni islands. It gave no detail beyond the names, so I couldn't confirm lodging quality.
